business_patterns.top_pattern: CA rare catastrophic and unclassifiable inpatient outliers
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / Inpatient rare catastrophic and unclassifiable cases

providers: HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH

key_driver_codes: Percutaneous Cardiovascular Procedures with Intraluminal Device without MCC
Intracranial Vascular Procedures with Principal Diagnosis of Hemorrhage with MCC
Heart Transplant or Implant of Heart Assist System without MCC
NONTRAUM SAH LT CAROTID SIPHON BIF
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA cost growth is being driven by a concentrated set of rare, very high-cost inpatient cases rather than a broad-based clinical trend. Much of the impact sits in unclassifiable or highly unusual admissions, with several individual episodes carrying extremely high paid amounts. This should be treated as a case-level catastrophic outlier pattern first, not as general utilization growth.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A few admissions can materially distort results, so the business risk is high if these cases are valid but unmanaged or invalid but miscoded.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a joint clinical and coding case audit on the top CA outlier admissions to confirm diagnosis and DRG assignment, then separate valid catastrophic cases from classification issues before taking broader provider action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The dollars are concentrated in a very small number of rare or unclassifiable admissions with low baseline and small admission counts.
evidence_summary: CA rare and unclassifiable clinical cases added about +$16.0M.
Three unclassifiable diagnoses alone contributed about +$7.2M: cervical cord lesion at C2 +$2.7M, other cirrhosis of liver +$2.6M, and dilated cardiomyopathy +$1.9M.
Several admissions carried extremely high paid per admit, including a heart transplant or heart assist episode at HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER of about +$1.4M.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is rising through both provider mix and authorization mix
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / ACUTE HOSPITAL / PPO and HMO

providers: HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH

business_patterns.pattern_details: CA acute hospital cost growth is showing up across both PPO and HMO, with authorized admissions carrying most of the dollars. The increase is coming from a mix of more admissions at O'CONNOR HOSPITAL and higher paid per admit at HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER and other concentrated providers. This is a provider-mix and authorization-mix problem, not a single-product issue.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the clearest operational cost lever in CA because both volume management and provider economics are contributing at the same time.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Compare CA acute hospital admissions by provider, product, and PA status, then send O'CONNOR HOSPITAL volume growth to UM review and HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER and HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH to reimbursement and network review for paid-per-admit pressure.
evidence_summary: CA PPO acute hospital authorized admissions added about +$5.8M, with 18 more admissions and paid per admit up about $81.1K.
CA HMO acute hospital added about +$1.8M, concentrated at HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER with 12 more admissions and paid per admit up about $118.3K.
O'CONNOR HOSPITAL drove about +$1.2M across PPO and HMO through 35 more admissions even as paid per admit fell.
Separate unit-cost-only pressure added about +$1.3M in CA acute hospital across PPO and HMO despite flat or lower admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA authorization-code movement must be validated before policy action
key_driver_codes: Other Digestive System Diagnoses with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: A material share of CA cost movement is tied to authorization-code distribution rather than a clear change in utilization or reimbursement. That means the first question is whether PA-required status, claim mapping, or classification changed. Business action on UM or reimbursement should wait until that mapping is reconciled.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If this is a mapping shift, acting on it as true medical cost trend would misdirect policy and provider interventions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Reconcile AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION to actual PA-required status and claims mapping in CA, especially for Aftercare with CC/MCC and HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER, before changing authorization rules or reimbursement policy.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is explicitly flagged as an auth or mapping shift that requires validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION added about +$4.4M and is flagged for validation before action.
Aftercare with CC/MCC accounts for about +$3.5M of the shift.
HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER contributes another about +$0.4M within the same authorization-code movement.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Post-acute inpatient settings are a major site-of-care cost driver
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: GA, VA, CA, IN / LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL and Physical Rehab / POS and PPO
business_patterns.pattern_details: Post-acute inpatient settings are producing a sizable share of the cost increase, especially LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL and Physical Rehab. The pattern reflects both more admissions and very high paid amounts per admit, with several episodes concentrated in aftercare and unclassifiable cases. This is a site-of-care and level-of-care management issue more than a broad acute hospital trend.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: LTCH and rehab placements can create large avoidable spend if admission criteria, length of stay, or discharge routing are not tightly managed.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit LTCH and rehab episodes for admission criteria, length of stay, and discharge pathway, then tighten UM escalation and network steerage where members could be managed in lower-cost post-acute settings.
evidence_summary: LTCH and Physical Rehab spend across GA, VA, CA, and IN added about +$7.8M.
GA LTCH unclassifiable cases added about +$2.9M on just 2 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $695.9K.
VA LTCH aftercare added about +$1.1M across 6 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $181.7K.
CA PPO Physical Rehab added about +$1.6M, and IN PPO LTCH added about +$1.6M including non-authorized unclassifiable cases.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorized PPO acute hospital pressure is recurring across multiple states
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CT, IN, KY, MO, NH, NV, VA, OH / ACUTE HOSPITAL / PPO

providers: HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH

business_patterns.pattern_details: Authorized PPO acute hospital spend is not isolated to one market. Across the listed states, the pattern shows recurring pressure from cervical spine, aftercare, and unclassifiable admissions, with both more admissions and higher paid per admit. OH adds a separate unit-cost-led PPO acute signal even with fewer admissions.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A repeated authorized acute hospital pattern across several states suggests a portable UM and reimbursement opportunity rather than a single local anomaly.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a state-by-state provider review of authorized PPO acute admissions, prioritizing cervical spinal fusion, aftercare, and unclassifiable cases in KY, CT, MO, and OH for inpatient appropriateness and paid-per-admit performance.
evidence_summary: Authorized PPO acute hospital spend across CT, IN, KY, MO, NH, NV, VA, and OH added about +$6.4M.
KY cervical spinal fusion added about +$1.0M with 18 more admissions, and CT cervical spinal fusion added about +$0.9M with 10 more admissions.
MO unclassifiable acute cases added about +$1.0M with paid per admit up about $74.8K, and HILLCREST MEDICAL CENTER in MO added about +$0.6M with paid per admit up about $95.8K.
OH shows a separate +$1.4M PPO acute unit-cost increase despite 3 fewer admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: NY cervical spine episodes are driving both clinical and operational growth
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: NY / Cervical spine inpatient episodes and EPO acute hospital
business_patterns.pattern_details: NY is showing a focused cervical spine pattern that appears in both clinical and operational views. Admissions are up for cervical spinal stenosis and cervical radiculopathy, and EPO acute hospital spend is rising on the same surgical family. This looks like a true specialty trend that should be managed at the episode level.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A concentrated spine trend is easier to act on than general medical trend because the clinical pathway, admission decision, and payment terms can all be targeted.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a NY cervical spine episode review that pairs surgical appropriateness and inpatient criteria review with EPO acute hospital payment review for cervical spinal fusion and related aftercare.
evidence_summary: NY cervical spine-related clinical and operational patterns added about +$4.5M.
Clinical cervical spinal stenosis added about +$2.2M with 22 more admissions, and cervical radiculopathy added about +$0.8M with 10 more admissions.
NY EPO acute hospital cervical spinal fusion added about +$1.0M with 11 more admissions and paid per admit up about $27.4K.
Aftercare with CC/MCC added another about +$0.5M in NY EPO acute hospital.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Small-volume provider and facility outliers are emerging outside the main markets
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CT, IN, NY, GA / Small-volume Children's, Critical Access, and acute provider outliers

providers: HALIFAX HEALTH MEDICAL CENTER OF DAYTONA BEACH

key_driver_codes: Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with CC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several smaller providers and facility types are showing emerging cost signals that are individually small but collectively meaningful. The pattern is concentrated in CHILDRENS, CRITICAL ACCESS, and low-volume acute providers, often tied to rare cases or a handful of additional admissions. These are better handled through targeted exception review than through broad policy changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Small-volume outliers can become recurring leakage if they are ignored, but they also carry high false-positive risk if treated as broad trend.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Place the named providers and cases into a targeted exception queue for case-level validation, medical necessity review, and provider-specific follow-up rather than enterprise-wide policy change.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most of the impact comes from low-baseline, small-volume providers and rare cases that need case-level confirmation before broader action.
evidence_summary: Small-volume provider and facility outliers across CT, IN, NY, and GA added about +$1.9M.
Rare CT, IN, and NY clinical outliers added about +$0.8M, including neuro cases at MANNING FAMILY CHILDREN'S and wound or respiratory cases at HARRISON COUNTY HOSPITAL.
CT PPO CHILDRENS activity at MANNING FAMILY CHILDREN'S added about +$0.4M with 7 more admissions and paid per admit up about $62.2K.
GA POS acute and IN PPO CRITICAL ACCESS activity added about +$0.7M from small-volume admission growth and higher paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA lower-acuity spine and aftercare episodes are rising in a focused cluster
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / Lower-acuity spine and post-surgical aftercare
key_driver_codes: SPINAL STENOSIS LUMBAR REGION NO NC
ENC SURG AFTRCARE FLW SURG CIRC SYS
business_patterns.pattern_details: Beyond the catastrophic CA outliers, there is a second CA clinical pattern in lower-acuity spine and post-surgical aftercare. The increase is concentrated in a limited set of diagnoses tied to aftercare and lumbar spine conditions rather than broad inpatient growth. This is best managed as an episode-pattern review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Focused aftercare and spine clusters can signal avoidable inpatient follow-up, longer stays, or poorly managed post-surgical pathways.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Review CA aftercare and lumbar spine admissions through episode management to confirm that post-surgical follow-up and lower-acuity spine cases are being managed in the right setting and duration.
evidence_summary: CA lower-acuity spine and aftercare cases added about +$1.2M.
Post-surgical circulatory aftercare added about +$0.4M with 3 more admissions and paid per admit up about $60.3K.
Lumbar stenosis and lumbar disc or radiculopathy together added about +$0.3M with 7 more admissions.

executive_summary.headline: Cost growth is concentrated in CA acute hospital authorization and provider mix, CA rare outlier admissions, post-acute site-of-care episodes, and one CA authorization mapping issue that must be validated first.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: The largest operational pressure comes from authorized acute hospital and post-acute inpatient patterns, especially in CA and across recurring PPO acute hospital segments. CA also has a material authorization-code distribution shift that should be treated as a gating validation issue before changing UM or reimbursement policy. After validation, the clearest business levers are provider-level acute hospital management in CA, tighter LTCH and rehab site-of-care control, and targeted cervical spine management in NY.
recommended_focus_order: Validate CA AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION before any authorization or reimbursement policy change.
Address CA acute hospital provider mix and rare high-cost inpatient admissions.
Tighten LTCH and rehab site-of-care management and launch focused NY cervical spine review.

notes: All 21 analytical groups were assigned to 8 business patterns.
Some lower-volume groups were intentionally merged when they shared the same business mechanism and downstream action.
Scope was left neutral for deterministic downstream reconciliation.
